html:
Juba is the capital and largest city of South Sudan, on the White Nile, which grew from a small British administrative and missionary town of the 1920s.

It was the main town of the south and a garrison through the civil wars, often besieged. After the peace of 2005 it became the seat of the southern government and grew fast with oil money, aid agencies and traders from Uganda and Kenya.

On 9 July 2011 it hosted the celebrations of the independence of South Sudan. Fighting broke out in the city in 2013 and 2016, part of the civil war. A planned new capital at Ramciel was never built.
sum: Juba is the capital and largest city of South Sudan, on the White Nile, which grew from a small British administrative and missionary town of the 1920s.
